title: Scalable Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Bidirectional Compression: Beyond Pessimistic Limits
summary: In centralized, distributed, and federated learning with stochastic gradients and $n$ workers, it was recently shown that it is infeasible to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point faster than $\tildeΩ\left(\min\left\{\frac{d κL Δ}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h L Δ}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h σ^2 L Δ}{n \varepsilon^2},\; \frac{h σ^2 L Δ}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{h L Δ}{\varepsilon}\right\}\right)$ seconds in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings under standard assumptions: $L$-smoothness, $σ^2$-bounded unbiased stochastic gradients, and lower boundedness of the function, i.e., $f(x) \geq f^*$ for…
